name: Lies, Lies, Lies

items.name: Fried-chicken clogs (KFC x Crocs)
items.fact: Crocs and KFC made a clog printed to look like fried chicken, with two charms shaped like drumsticks that really smelled of fried chicken. They were first shown at New York Fashion Week in 2020.

items.name: Mac and cheese ice cream (Kraft x Van Leeuwen)
items.fact: In 2021 the New York ice-cream maker Van Leeuwen worked with Kraft on an ice cream that tastes of Kraft Macaroni & Cheese: bright orange, cheesy, salty and sweet at the same time.

items.name: Crisp-packet handbag (Balenciaga x Lay's)
items.fact: In 2022 the Paris fashion house Balenciaga sold a leather clutch bag made to look exactly like a packet of Lay's crisps, in several flavours, for about $1,800.

items.name: Marshmallow cola (Pepsi x Peeps)
items.fact: Pepsi worked with Peeps, the sugary American marshmallow sweets shaped like little chicks, on a limited-edition cola that tasted of marshmallow. It was sold for a short time around Easter.

items.name: Sausage-roll fashion (Greggs x Primark)
items.fact: Greggs, the British bakery chain famous for its sausage rolls, made a clothing collection with the fashion chain Primark, including hoodies and hats. Primark even opened a Greggs café inside one of its stores.

items.name: Gummy-bear trainers (Vans x Haribo)
items.fact: The skate-shoe brand Vans and the German sweet maker Haribo made a collection of trainers and clothes in the bright colours of Haribo's sweets, decorated with little gummy bears.

items.name: Cola biscuits (Coca-Cola x Oreo)
items.fact: Coca-Cola and Oreo swapped flavours: Oreo made biscuits with a Coca-Cola-flavoured filling that fizzed with popping candy, and Coca-Cola made a limited-edition drink that tasted of Oreo biscuits.

items.name: A robot cat dressed as an ox (Gucci x Doraemon)
items.fact: For the Year of the Ox in 2021, Gucci made a collection with Doraemon, the blue robot cat from a Japanese cartoon, who appeared dressed as an ox on bags, jumpers and trainers.

items.name: Pixel crocodile (Lacoste x Minecraft)
items.fact: The French tennis-shirt brand Lacoste made a clothing collection with the video game Minecraft, in which its famous green crocodile logo was redrawn in big square pixels.

items.name: Flamin' Hot fashion (Cheetos x Forever 21)
items.fact: In 2019 the snack brand Cheetos and the fashion chain Forever 21 launched a clothing line printed with Cheetos packets and Chester Cheetah, the brand's cartoon cheetah, in bright orange and red.

fakes.name: Bakery-scented hiking boots
fakes.fact: A German bakery chain and a hiking-boot maker made boots with insoles that smell of fresh bread. “The smell of the bakery on every mountain,” said the advert. The smell lasts about three months.

fakes.name: Espresso-scented car
fakes.fact: A Swedish coffee roaster and a car maker made a special-edition car whose air vents smell of fresh espresso every time you start the engine. Only 500 were made.

fakes.name: Sardine-tin phone case
fakes.fact: A Portuguese sardine brand and a phone-case maker made phone cases that look exactly like a tin of sardines. The ring-pull on the back opens a small mirror.

fakes.name: Gouda skateboards
fakes.fact: A Dutch cheese maker and a skateboard brand made skateboards from the same wood as its cheese boards, with a giant wheel of Gouda printed underneath. They sold out in Amsterdam in a day.

fakes.name: Mustard wellies
fakes.fact: A French mustard maker and a British welly-boot brand made rubber boots in the exact yellow of Dijon mustard. They were sold in a box shaped like a mustard jar.

fakes.name: Chilli hand cream
fakes.fact: A Mexican hot-sauce brand and a Spanish cosmetics company made a hand cream with a little chilli in it, to warm your fingers in winter. The tube warns: “Do not touch your eyes.”

fakes.name: Vacuum-cleaner handbag
fakes.fact: A German vacuum-cleaner maker and an Italian fashion house made a handbag with a tiny built-in vacuum for sucking up crumbs inside it. It cost €2,200 and had to be charged every night.

fakes.name: Toothpaste ice cream
fakes.fact: A Danish dairy and a toothpaste brand made a strong mint ice cream “for after dinner”. Each tub came with a small wooden toothbrush instead of a spoon.

fakes.name: Snooker-table trousers
fakes.fact: A British snooker-table maker and a London tailor made smart green trousers from real snooker-table cloth. The tailor says they are almost impossible to crease.

fakes.name: Shortbread-tin speaker
fakes.fact: A Scottish shortbread maker and a Danish speaker brand put a Bluetooth speaker inside a tartan shortbread tin, with a small space at the bottom for real biscuits.

fake: Give it a catchy name, maybe with “Brand x Brand” in brackets.
Two very different kinds of company, and where they're from.
The product: shoes, clothes, food, a gadget.
What makes it strange: a smell, a flavour, a look.
A year, a price, how fast it sold out.
A number, a place or a small problem it still has.
tips: Be specific: numbers, dates and real places make a lie believable.
Give it a small problem (“the smell wore off after a week”): perfect things sound fake.
Make both talks the same length and give them the same confidence.
Don't laugh. Decide now who says which one.
